owner_statement: D-P5.3-PLAN-AUTH: I, mayank-admin, authorize planning, read-only repository analysis, and official primary-source research only for P5.3 Camera And Live Monitoring Workspace. The authorized planning scope includes camera catalogue, camera detail, stream health, capability and probe views; single-camera and multi-camera live workspaces; monitor-wall layouts; browser-safe playback-session contracts; HLS/MSE and provisional WebRTC/WHEP transport evaluation; browser and codec capability detection; generated-only synthetic-media strategy; C1/C4/C10 validation methodology; low-resource, enhanced-workstation, control-room, GPU-lab, and future-server profiles; automatic stream admission, quality selection, backpressure, reconnect, stall detection, fallback, teardown, logout, and department-scope transitions; layout and preference storage contracts; accessibility and authoritative non-video alternatives; operator workflows and incident handoffs; typed API, event, pagination, freshness, concurrency, and error contracts; security and privacy threat analysis; dependency evaluation; producer-gap inventory; owner decision options; and a bounded P5.3 implementation and start plan. Planning must preserve the accepted Phase 2 camera and capability boundaries, the isolated Phase 2.5 Sentinel lab boundary, the Phase 3 dynamic hardware-profile architecture, the Phase 5 shared application foundation, and the P5.2 Command/GIS integration contracts. Low-resource mode must remain functionally complete, while capable hardware may increase stream count, resolution, frame rate, rendering quality, and acceleration without changing operator authority or security policy. Internet research is limited to official primary browser, media, WebRTC, WHEP, HLS, security, accessibility, and standards sources. Local planning documentation, generated/static planning validation, and one local checkpoint commit without push are authorized. This does not authorize product or test implementation, dependency installation or lockfile changes, source import, backend routes or migrations, frontend or media runtime, playback-session issuance, real providers or network access, Sentinel access, cameras or media, recording, snapshots, downloads, exports, Government or private data, models, datasets, artifacts or inference, operational actions, containers, Kubernetes, deployment, P5.4, or remote Git.
